extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and counsel involved in practitioner discipline/resignation proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing approval of a practitioner Resignation Affidavit under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and the resulting exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO (including limited wind‑up recognition, publication, notice, and reinstatement consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation is voluntary and aware
rubrics_metrics.description: The Resignation Affidavit must state that the resignation is freely and voluntarily rendered; the practitioner is not being subjected to coercion or duress; and the practitioner is fully aware of the implications of submitting the resignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the affidavit: 'His resignation is freely and voluntarily rendered; he is not being subjected to coercion or duress; and he is fully aware of the implications of submitting his resignation.' The Director approves only when the affidavit complies with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge subject of inquiry and allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must acknowledge in the Resignation Affidavit that he/she is the subject of an inquiry by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline and identify the matter (e.g., criminal case and guilty plea) underlying the inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from this case: the affidavit acknowledges the practitioner's guilty plea in United States v. Brien Santarlas and the nature of the charges (securities fraud conspiracy and securities fraud).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement-presumption acknowledgement (§11.60 consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that if the practitioner applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the facts upon which the matter is based are true and (ii) the practitioner could not have successfully defended against the potential violations under investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner must be aware of and accept this limited presumption when consenting to exclusion via a resignation affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for exclusion: criminal conviction / guilty plea
rubrics_metrics.description: A criminal conviction or a guilty plea (e.g., to securities fraud conspiracy and securities fraud) and the factual admissions in a plea allocution can constitute the factual basis for exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This order predicates exclusion upon the respondent's December 10, 2009 guilty plea and the plea allocution describing unlawful acts (accessing confidential information, passing it to others, and receiving cash).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline under §10.23(b)(3) — moral turpitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude is a ground for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Exclusion on Consent expressly states exclusion for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) by engaging in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline under §10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation is a ground for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Exclusion on Consent expressly states exclusion for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) by engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory/regulatory basis for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions approving a resignation affidavit and ordering exclusion on consent are taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority, specifically 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutes and regulations as the basis for approving the resignation affidavit and ordering exclusion and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for winding up client business
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon approval of the resignation affidavit, the practitioner may be granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for a specified short period (here, thirty (30) days) solely for the purpose of winding up all client business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order: 'granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for a period of thirty (30) days ... for the sole purpose of winding up all client business.' Limited recognition begins and expires on the dates specified in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to wind up matters and withdraw under §10.40 during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period of limited recognition the practitioner must wind up all client business before the Office and withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit duty during limited recognition: wind up client business and effect withdrawals consistent with § 10.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: While exercising limited recognition to wind up business, the practitioner shall not accept any new clients having business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order expressly states: 'Respondent ... shall not accept any new clients having business before the Office' during limited recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion on consent, the practitioner's identity, registration number, the basis for exclusion, and statutory/regulatory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires publication at: http://des.uspto.gov/FinalOEDReadingRoom.jsp and a Notice of Exclusion on Consent in the Official Gazette with specified content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (§11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State(s) where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs the OED Director to provide these notices as part of the discipline process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with obligations while excluded (§11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: While excluded from practice before the Office, the practitioner must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded;' practitioners should consult § 11.58 for the specific obligations applicable during exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures and consequences (§11.60 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any future request for reinstatement must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, including the consequences and presumptions acknowledged in the resignation affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.' The affidavit's presumption regarding facts and inability to defend applies for reinstatement consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the practitioner shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states both parties will bear their own costs; this is part of the terms of agreement for exclusion on consent.
